subject: First-packet SLO, chunk rhythm & pilot action items
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@atrialabs.com>, Timothy Lee <tim.lee@atrialabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT and streaming requirements (recap & pilot asks)

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Appreciate the clear context on your client constraints and expected load.

Call summary (high level)
- Target workload: conversational assistant (avg 40 tokens per response, multimodal attachments later).
- Peak patterns: 200 rps steady-state, short bursts up to ~600 rps for marketing pushes.
- Client types: mobile first (iOS/Android) with long-lived connections for streaming.

Performance / SLO asks we discussed
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): goal P50 <= 120 ms, P95 <= 300 ms for streaming start-of-response.
- Steady throughput: 200 rps sustained, concurrency ~50 active streams; burst capacity to ~600 rps.
- Chunk cadence: prefer 80–150 ms between chunks for interactive feel (small chunks, ~8–40 tokens per chunk).
- Streaming transport: SSE preferred for simplicity (client only needs EventSource). WebSocket allowed as fallback for bi-di activities.
- Fallbacks: when capacity constrained, automatic degrade to shorter responses + background completion (we can configure).

Pilot plan (asks from Atria Labs)
1) Share representative prompt set (10–20 prompts + expected token ranges) — this will drive our probe accuracy.
2) Provide recent traffic shape (5-minute bins) for a typical weekday and a marketing-burst day.
3) Confirm whether SSE is acceptable for your mobile app; if not, detail WebSocket requirements.

Attachments included: streaming-probe-results.csv (preliminary probe we ran against a similar model), packet-latency-snapshot.png, MA-sla-draft.pdf (for procurement).

Next steps / timeline
- If you can share prompts & traffic by EOD Tue, we’ll run a 48-hour pilot probe in our Dedicated sandbox and come back with measured P50/P95 TTFT and chunk cadence behavior.
- Goal: pilot kickoff within 72 hours after we have prompts.

Questions for you (quick)
- Are there any regulatory constraints we should know about (retention, key management)?
- Do you want canary on 5% of production traffic for the pilot or isolated traffic replay?

Thanks — I’ll track action items and loop legal/procurement once you confirm the MA approach.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

(attachment: streaming-probe-results.csv)

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@atrialabs.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Timothy Lee <tim.lee@atrialabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT and streaming requirements (recap & pilot asks)

Thanks Dev — very clear, appreciate the write-up. A few clarifications from our side: we prefer SSE where possible (mobile EventSource on our wrapper), however we need a WebSocket fallback for older Android devices (enterprise images).

On TTFT: our internal product team would like to push the P95 target to <= 350 ms if that gives you more headroom for concurrency/throughput. Is P95 <= 350 ms a reasonable contractual target for the pilot?

Payload sizes: most responses are small (avg 350 bytes JSON), occasional larger payloads with image URLs. We will provide a prompt set by EOD tomorrow.

Security: we are using customer-managed keys (KMS) and will need to validate key rotation and audit logs during the pilot — can you include a brief checklist of what you’ll surface in the pilot logs?

Also — are there rate-limiting headers we should expect in the probe responses (we’d like to wire automated client backoff).

Best,
Aisha
VP Product, Atria Labs
aisha.khan@atrialabs.com

On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 15:02, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT and streaming requirements (recap & pilot asks)

Couple of internal notes / proposed approach from Sales/PD:
- Pilot routing: run the probe in an isolated Dedicated sandbox with a canary option (we can mirror production traffic) — run both SSE and WS paths to validate client compatibility.
- Model variant: recommend using a quantized 8-bit performance variant (balanced latency/cost) for the pilot; keep a smaller higher-quality variant for canary fallback.
- Observability: ensure we surface TTFT P50/P95, chunk cadence histogram (ms between emits), active concurrent streams, and token/sec metrics. Those map directly to our Console dashboards.
- Commercial: propose a time-bound pilot T&Cs in the attached MA-sla-draft.pdf. If Atria wants P95 <= 350ms as contractual, we can accept for the pilot with a clause that production SLA will be scoped after 14-day baseline.

Action: Dev — please capture the probe checklist Ben describes and confirm the scheduling window. Marissa — can you prep a quick cost estimate for a 48-hour probe on a dedicated pool (include burst headroom)?

—Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MA-sla-draft.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT and streaming requirements (recap & pilot asks)

Adding a couple of operational asks before we kick off the probe:
1) Test harness & credentials: we need an API key for Atria’s replay, plus client cert thumbprints if they want mTLS.
2) Test dataset: we need the 10–20 prompt seed set and an example response for size estimation.

Quick snippet from streaming-probe-results.csv (prelim) — we saw these chunk intervals on a baseline run against a similar workload:
- run_20270528, p50_chunk_ms=95, p95_chunk_ms=210, avg_tokens_per_chunk=18
- run_20270528, ttft_p50_ms=110, ttft_p95_ms=280

Marissa: I can own scheduling the 1-hr pilot kickoff (ops + eng + Atria) once Dev confirms the final date. Ben — I’ll need that cost estimate to put on the pilot sheet.

(attachment: packet-latency-snapshot.png)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@atrialabs.com>, Timothy Lee <tim.lee@atrialabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT and streaming requirements (recap & pilot asks)

Thanks all — consolidated action items and schedule below. Forwarding the pilot plan + MA link to procurement.

Confirmed items
- Transport: primary SSE, WebSocket fallback for older Android.
- Contractual pilot target: TTFT P95 <= 350 ms for the 48-hour pilot window (as requested by Atria). Production SLA to be scoped after baseline.
- Throughput: probe will exercise 200 rps steady, up to 600 rps burst for short windows.
- Concurrency: target 50 active streams, will validate up to 120 concurrency during burst.
- Chunk cadence: target 80–150 ms between chunks; acceptance threshold p95_chunk_ms <= 250 ms.

Pilot kickoff: Friday 4 Jun 2027, 10:00 AM PT — 1 hour. (Marissa to send calendar invite).

Deliverables within first 48 hours of probe
- TTFT P50/P95, per-route chunk cadence histograms, concurrency heatmap, per-token cost estimate, and KMS/audit log sample for verification.
- Fallback policy: automatic degrade to 2-3 chunk summary mode if P95 exceeds threshold; collect examples for QA.

Open asks for Atria (please confirm by EOD Thu)
- Provide the 10–20 prompt seed set + traffic shape for probe.
- Confirm whether you prefer canary (5% live traffic) or isolated replay.

Once we have the prompts, Ben & Marissa will finalize cost and contract items and I’ll spin up the dedicated probe environment. If that all looks good, I’ll attach the MA for signature and we’ll proceed with the kickoff on Friday.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MA-sla-draft.pdf)
